qa.question: Should East Bend unit 2 planned retirement be 2039 instead of 2038?
qa.finding: The 2024 Duke Energy Kentucky plan (https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2024-00197/e.rolfes-adkins%40duke-energy.com/09092024025857/DEK_IRP_PUBLIC_06212024.pdf) says dual fuel operation from 2030 and a combined cycle replacement by 2039. A table in the plan reads retire in 2039 for the co-firing option. I found no document that says 2038.
qa.recommendation: Check the source of 2038. If none exists, change Planned retire to 2039 and cite the 2024 plan.
qa.note: The plan also studies retiring in 2032 or 2036 in other cases, but the preferred portfolio keeps the unit to 2039.

qa.question: Does the federal funding note for East Bend unit 2 apply to the conversion?
qa.finding: The Department of Energy page (https://www.energy.gov/hgeo/defense-production-act-title-iii-project-selections-coal-fleet-projects-and-west-gateway) lists 33,400,000 dollars for the East Bend Coal Reliability Assurance Initiative. It covers steam turbine and boiler economizer work to keep the coal unit running. It does not mention diesel or gas.
qa.recommendation: Keep the note but add that the funding is for coal reliability work, not the conversion.
qa.note: The note is a running log, so a person adds the clarifying line above the old text.
